content: Butoconazole vaginal cream is a medication used to treat yeast infections in the vagina. It may also be prescribed for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available as a cream that is inserted into the vagina. It is typically used once daily at bedtime for either 1 day or 6 days, depending on your prescription. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use butoconazole exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed. To use the vaginal cream, follow these steps: 1. Fill the applicator provided with the cream to the indicated level. 2. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart. 3. Insert the applicator high into your vagina (unless you are pregnant). If you are pregnant, insert the applicator gently. If you encounter resistance or difficulty inserting it, stop and contact your doctor. 4. Push the plunger to release the medication. 5. Remove the applicator and discard it. 6. Wash your hands thoroughly to prevent spreading the infection. Apply the dose when you are lying down to go to bed. The medication works best if you remain lying down after application, except to wash your hands. You may want to wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Do not douche unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using butoconazole even if your symptoms improve. Do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. You should also continue using this medication during your menstrual period. Before using butoconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if: You are allergic to butoconazole or any other medications. You are taking any prescription or nonprescription drugs, especially antibiotics or vitamins. You have a history of diabetes, immune system problems, HIV infection, or AIDS. You are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using butoconazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, insert it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not insert a double dose to make up for a missed one. Butoconazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Burning sensation in the vagina when the cream is applied. Irritation in the vagina when the cream is applied. Stomach pain. Fever. Foul-smelling vaginal discharge. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not freeze the medication. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Butoconazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow it. Refrain from sexual intercourse while using this medication. An ingredient in the cream may weaken latex products such as condoms or diaphragms, so do not use these products within 72 hours of applying the cream. Wear clean cotton underwear or underwear with a cotton crotch, and avoid synthetic fabrics like nylon or rayon. Do not share this medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor. The brand name for butoconazole is Gynazole-1®.
